title: Canonical obstruction to lifting a complex across a square-zero quotient
statement:
Let $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ be a surjection of commutative rings with kernel $J$ satisfying $J^2=0$, regarded as an $R$-module by multiplication. Use the derived category of ordinary modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D^-(R)$ for its objects with $H^i=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$, and $-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ for the total tensor of K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For every $C\in D^-(R)$ there is a canonical morphism
$$\omega_{R'/R}(C):C\longrightarrow(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}J)[2].$$
It vanishes if and only if there exists $C'\in D^-(R')$ with an isomorphism $C'\otimes_{R'}^{\mathbf L}R\cong C$. It is natural in $C$: for $u:C\to D$ one has $\omega(D)u=(u\otimes1)[2]\omega(C)$. For any flat ring map $R'\to U'$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], set $U=U'\otimes_{R'}R$ and $J_U=JU'$. Under the canonical identifications $J\otimes_R U\cong J_U$ and $(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}J)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}U\cong(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}U)\otimes_U^{\mathbf L}J_U$, the scalar extension of $\omega_{R'/R}(C)$ equals $\omega_{U'/U}(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}U)$. Here ordinary tensor products and their canonical maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0DYR, lemma-canonical-class-algebra, (1)-(3); its proof produces a bounded-above free lift. The base-change clause here is restricted to flat R′→U′.

proof.text: Choose a complex $K$ representing $C$. Choose $b$ with $H^i(C)=0$ for $i>b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology] the inclusion $\tau_{\le b}K\to K$ of the chosen complex $K$ induces isomorphisms on $H^i$ for $i\le b$, and both sides have $H^i=0$ for $i>b$, so it is a quasi-isomorphism; and $(\tau_{\le b}K)^n=0$ for $n>b$. Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] to ordinary $R$-modules, the class of all free modules (it contains the zero module, and the free module on the underlying set surjects onto any module), $a=b$ and $\tau_{\le b}K$. Composing gives a free complex $P$ with $P^n=0$ for $n>b$, a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K$, and hence an isomorphism $QP\cong C$. A map from a free module lifts across a surjection by lifting the images of its basis; tensoring an exact sequence with a free module gives a direct sum of copies of it, which is exact. Thus its terms are projective and flat. By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], $P$ is K-flat, so $P\otimes_R J$ represents $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}J$.

Write $P^n=R^{(B_n)}$ and take $F^n=R'^{(B_n)}$, with $B_n$ empty above the bound. The basis identifies $JF^n=J^{(B_n)}=P^n\otimes_R J$ and $F^n/JF^n=P^n$. Lift each $d_P^n$ to $d'^n:F^n\to F^{n+1}$ by choosing lifts of the finitely supported image of each basis vector. The composite $d'^{n+1}d'^n$ lands in $JF^{n+2}$, since its reduction is zero, and kills $JF^n$, since it is $R'$-linear and $J^2=0$. It therefore induces $w_P^n:P^n\to P^{n+2}\otimes_R J$. Associativity gives $d'^{n+2}(d'^{n+1}d'^n)=(d'^{n+2}d'^{n+1})d'^n$. Restriction of $d'$ to $JF$ is $d_P\otimes1$, hence $(d_P^{n+2}\otimes1)w_P^n=w_P^{n+1}d_P^n$. Thus $w_P:P\to(P\otimes_R J)[2]$ is a chain map (the shift by two has positive differential), using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the tensor maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

For a chain map $a:P\to V$ between bounded-above free models, lift its components to $a'^n:F^n\to G^n$ as above, where $e'$ lifts the differential of $V$. The defect $b'^n=e'^na'^n-a'^{n+1}d'^n$ reduces to zero and kills $JF^n$; denote its factor $b^n:P^n\to V^{n+1}\otimes_R J$. Expanding and cancelling the middle terms gives
$$e'^{n+1}b'^n+b'^{n+1}d'^n=e'^{n+1}e'^na'^n-a'^{n+2}d'^{n+1}d'^n.$$
On the ideal submodules this is exactly
$$w_V^na^n-(a^{n+2}\otimes1)w_P^n=(d_V^{n+1}\otimes1)b^n+b^{n+1}d_P^n.$$
The right side is the chain-homotopy formula for maps to $(V\otimes_R J)[2]$, with homotopy component $b^n$ landing in its degree $n-1$. Therefore the two maps agree after localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Free terms are projective by the basis-lifting argument in Step 1. Consequently [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] represents every derived morphism between the free models by a chain map and identifies equality with chain homotopy. Apply Step 3 to such a representative to obtain naturality. Apply it to the identity chain map with two different choices of graded lifts and lifted differentials to obtain independence of those choices. For two models of the same $C$, represent their derived comparison isomorphism by a chain map using the same bijection; its tensor with $J$ is the derived tensor of that comparison, since both models are K-flat. Step 3 then identifies their classes under the prescribed comparisons with $C$ and $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}J$. This defines the canonical morphism $\omega_{R'/R}(C)$ and proves $\omega(D)u=(u\otimes1)[2]\omega(C)$ for every $u:C\to D$.

Suppose $\omega(C)=0$. The injectivity in [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative], applied to the bounded-above projective source $P$ and target $(P\otimes_R J)[2]$, makes $w_P$ null-homotopic. Thus there are $g^n:P^n\to P^{n+1}\otimes_R J$ with
$$w_P^n=(d_P^{n+1}\otimes1)g^n+g^{n+1}d_P^n.$$
Let $\widetilde g^n:F^n\to F^{n+1}$ be the composite through $P^n$, then $g^n$, then $JF^{n+1}\subset F^{n+1}$. It kills $JF^n$ and lands in $JF^{n+1}$, so $\widetilde g^{n+1}\widetilde g^n=0$. For $D^n=d'^n-\widetilde g^n$, expansion yields
$$D^{n+1}D^n=d'^{n+1}d'^n-d'^{n+1}\widetilde g^n-\widetilde g^{n+1}d'^n=0$$
by the displayed homotopy equation and the identifications of Step 2. Therefore $(F,D)$ is a bounded-above free $R'$-complex reducing exactly to $P$. By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] over $R'$, its ordinary reduction computes derived reduction. Its image $C'\in D^-(R')$ has $C'\otimes_{R'}^{\mathbf L}R\cong C$.

Conversely suppose $C'\in D^-(R')$ with $C'\otimes_{R'}^{\mathbf L}R\cong C$. The truncation and free-resolution argument of Step 1 over $R'$, by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology] and [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] for the class of free $R'$-modules, gives a bounded-above free representative $F$ of $C'$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], so $F\otimes_{R'}R$ is a bounded-above free representative of $C$. In constructing its obstruction choose $F$ itself and its genuine differential. Its consecutive differentials compose to zero; all curvature components are zero. Independence of choices from Step 4 now gives $\omega(C)=0$.

Let $R'\to U'$ be flat and $U=U'/JU'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], tensoring $0\to J\to R'\to R\to0$ with $U'$ gives $0\to J\otimes_{R'}U'\to U'\to U\to0$. Its first image is $J_U=JU'$, whose square is zero. The balancing relations in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] identify $J\otimes_{R'}U'$ with $J\otimes_R U$: $j\otimes u'$ maps to $j\otimes\bar u'$, with inverse given by lifting $\bar u'$; changing a lift by $JU'$ contributes zero because $J^2=0$. For every $R$-module $N$ the same balancing gives $N\otimes_R U\cong N\otimes_{R'}U'$. Hence $U$ is flat over $R$ by the injection criterion [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Flat tensor exactness identifies kernels, images and their quotients after tensoring, so tensoring complexes with $U$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Thus termwise tensor with $U$ computes derived tensor with $U$.

Use the models $P,F,d'$ of Step 2. The complex $P_U=P\otimes_R U$ is bounded-above free over $U$, and $F_U^n=F^n\otimes_{R'}U'$ with differential lifts $d'^n\otimes1$ is a choice for its obstruction construction. On each basis vector, $(d'^{n+1}\otimes1)(d'^n\otimes1)=(d'^{n+1}d'^n)\otimes1$, so the resulting curvature is $w_P\otimes_R1_U$ under $J\otimes_R U\cong J_U$ from Step 7. The chain isomorphism
$$(P\otimes_R J)\otimes_R U\longrightarrow(P\otimes_R U)\otimes_U J_U,\qquad (p\otimes j)\otimes u\longmapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes ju$$
has inverse $(p\otimes u)\otimes(j\otimes v)\mapsto(p\otimes j)\otimes uv$; both are well-defined by the balancing relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and commute with differentials. By Step 7 the left side computes the scalar extension of $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}J$; by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] for $P_U$, the right side computes $(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}U)\otimes_U^{\mathbf L}J_U$. The degree-two shift introduces no sign. This is exactly the asserted canonical scalar-extension equality, now independent of choices by Step 4.
